fields.name: AI Quant Research: 12-Week Transition
fields.description: From senior Python market-data and trading systems engineer to quantitative ML research: statistics, microstructure, rigorous validation, PyTorch, execution-aware backtesting and a publishable portfolio.

fields.title: Statistics for quantitative research
fields.deliverable: Notebook: statistical analysis of returns and significance tests

fields.topic_name: Probability distributions, expectation, variance, covariance
fields.description:
Study guide: Study common return distributions (normal, Student-t, empirical), moments, skew and kurtosis; estimate rolling covariance and explain fat tails.

Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/tutorial/stats.html

fields.topic_name: Conditional probability, Bayes’ theorem, hypothesis tests
fields.description:
Study guide: Derive Bayes' rule and null/alternative hypotheses; use scipy.stats tests on a proposed imbalance signal and distinguish p-value from effect size.

Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/tutorial/stats/hypothesis_tests.html

fields.topic_name: Confidence intervals, bootstrapping and multiple testing
fields.description:
Study guide: Compute t-based and bootstrap confidence intervals; run many simulated tests to illustrate false discoveries and apply FDR control.

Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html

fields.topic_name: Analyze market-return distributions
fields.description:
Study guide: Calculate log returns from public time-ordered prices; plot histogram, QQ plot, volatility clustering and summary statistics without future leakage.

Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/tutorial/stats.html

fields.topic_name: Test whether a simple signal’s expected return differs from zero
fields.description:
Study guide: Form a directional-signal hypothesis; calculate next-period returns, use dependence-aware uncertainty and report effect size plus uncertainty, not just p-value.

Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/tutorial/stats/hypothesis_tests.html

fields.topic_name: Stationarity, autocorrelation, heteroskedasticity
fields.description:
Study guide: Run ADF carefully and inspect ACF/PACF; compare raw price, returns and absolute returns and explain volatility clustering.

Reference: https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/tsa.html

fields.topic_name: Bid/ask spread, mid-price, microprice, depth and imbalance
fields.description:
Study guide: Reconstruct top-of-book state; compute spread, midprice, microprice and level-1 imbalance, guarding against zero or invalid quote sizes.

Reference: https://lobsterdata.com/info/DataStructure.php

fields.topic_name: Market regimes, event time vs. clock time
fields.description:
Study guide: Compare event-time bars with calendar-time bars; characterize low/high volatility regimes and define features strictly from available history.

Reference: https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/tsa.html

fields.topic_name: Implement rolling volatility, ACF and order-book imbalance
fields.description:
Study guide: Implement time-indexed rolling realized volatility, autocorrelation and imbalance in pandas/NumPy; unit-test boundaries and timestamp ordering.

Reference: https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/tsa.html

fields.topic_name: Visualize signal behavior across different volatility regimes
fields.description:
Study guide: Plot regime-conditioned distributions of imbalance, volatility and forward returns; comment on stability and sample sizes.

Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/tutorial/stats.html

fields.topic_name: Linear and logistic regression, regularization
fields.description:
Study guide: Fit regularized logistic regression to directional labels; understand coefficients, scaling, class balance and L1/L2 penalties.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/supervised_learning.html

fields.topic_name: Decision trees, random forests, XGBoost
fields.description:
Study guide: Train random forest and XGBoost on the same features; compare complexity, generalization and feature importance without touching test labels.

Reference: https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/

fields.topic_name: Classification metrics and probability calibration
fields.description:
Study guide: Measure balanced accuracy, precision/recall, ROC-AUC and Brier score; draw reliability curves and inspect probability calibration.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html

fields.topic_name: Create directional labels over several prediction horizons
fields.description:
Study guide: Define up/down/flat labels from future midprice at fixed event and clock horizons; specify neutral thresholds and exclude incomplete trailing labels.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html

fields.topic_name: Train a naive baseline and logistic regression model
fields.description:
Study guide: Train majority-class and last-move baselines plus logistic regression; evaluate on a held-out later time interval with confusion matrix.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/supervised_learning.html

fields.topic_name: Chronological train/validation/test splits
fields.description:
Study guide: Partition observations chronologically into train, validation and untouched test; explain why random K-fold leaks temporal structure.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html

fields.topic_name: Walk-forward testing, overlapping labels, purging and embargoes
fields.description:
Study guide: Create walk-forward folds and account for overlap between forward-return label windows using purging and optional embargo; audit index ranges.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html

fields.topic_name: Feature leakage, selection bias, overfitting
fields.description:
Study guide: List failure cases (future rolling statistics, normalization on full data, tuned test thresholds, repeated trials) and add automated leakage assertions.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html

fields.topic_name: Implement a walk-forward evaluation framework
fields.description:
Study guide: Implement an expanding/rolling walk-forward evaluator with timestamp cutoffs, isolated preprocessing and per-fold metrics.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html

fields.topic_name: Compare random split against proper chronological validation
fields.description:
Study guide: Evaluate identical features with shuffled vs chronological splits; explain optimistic inflation and document reproducible seed and dates.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html

fields.title: LOB feature research
fields.deliverable: Feature-research report with stable and unstable signals

fields.topic_name: Order-book imbalance and microprice
fields.description:
Study guide: Derive and code level-1 / multi-level imbalance and microprice; test monotonicity and behavior with empty or crossed books.

Reference: https://lobsterdata.com/info/DataStructure.php

fields.topic_name: Order-flow imbalance, liquidity shifts, spread and depth
fields.description:
Study guide: Study order-flow imbalance based on quote changes and trade events; distinguish displayed depth, cancellations and true aggressive flow.

Reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.6402

fields.topic_name: Feature importance, ablation and stability
fields.description:
Study guide: Compare permutation importance with ablation; rerun over separate chronological windows and watch for correlated or unstable features.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/permutation_importance.html

fields.topic_name: Engineer 10–20 candidate features from available data
fields.description:
Study guide: Implement 10–20 timestamp-safe candidate features such as spread, depth ratios, lagged returns and rolling OFI with NaN handling.

Reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.6402

fields.topic_name: Run feature ablations using logistic regression and XGBoost
fields.description:
Study guide: Fit logistic and XGBoost baselines; remove feature groups and compare out-of-sample metrics with uncertainty intervals.

Reference: https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/

fields.topic_name: Tensors, autograd, GPU computation
fields.description:
Study guide: Practice tensor shapes, CPU/GPU placement and autograd; implement a differentiable linear model and inspect parameter gradients.

Reference: https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/basics/intro.html

fields.topic_name: Optimizers, training loops, regularization
fields.description:
Study guide: Build explicit training/validation loops with BCE loss, Adam, weight decay, early stopping and fixed random seeds.

Reference: https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/basics/intro.html

fields.topic_name: Dataset/DataLoader design and reproducibility
fields.description:
Study guide: Create a PyTorch Dataset with time-ordered feature windows and a DataLoader; prevent windows from crossing train/test boundaries.

Reference: https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/basics/data_tutorial.html

fields.topic_name: Implement an MLP for market direction forecasting
fields.description:
Study guide: Train a compact MLP on normalized lagged market features; log epoch losses, validation metrics, checkpoint and runtime.

Reference: https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/basics/intro.html

fields.topic_name: Benchmark PyTorch against your classical ML baselines
fields.description:
Study guide: Compare MLP to logistic and XGBoost on exactly matching data splits, features and decision metrics; include throughput and latency.

Reference: https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/basics/intro.html

fields.topic_name: LSTM and GRU models
fields.description:
Study guide: Explain recurrent hidden states and gating; implement LSTM/GRU input shapes and assess overfitting on financial sequences.

Reference: https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.LSTM.html

fields.topic_name: Attention and positional information
fields.description:
Study guide: Read scaled dot-product attention and positional encodings; implement a small attention example and discuss causal masks.

Reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

fields.topic_name: Sequence windows and nonstationary data
fields.description:
Study guide: Construct time-aligned lookback windows with forward prediction horizons; avoid cross-session contamination and missing-event artifacts.

Reference: https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/basics/data_tutorial.html

fields.topic_name: Train a compact LSTM on feature sequences
fields.description:
Study guide: Fit a small LSTM with early stopping to sequences of microstructure features and report held-out performance.

Reference: https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.LSTM.html

fields.topic_name: Compare performance against XGBoost under identical splits
fields.description:
Study guide: Use identical folds, labels, costs and scoring to compare LSTM against XGBoost; discuss whether added complexity is justified.

Reference: https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/

fields.title: Research rigor and statistical significance
fields.deliverable: Research memo: which results survive rigorous evaluation?

fields.topic_name: Block bootstrap and dependence-aware uncertainty
fields.description:
Study guide: Implement moving-block bootstrap of serially dependent returns or scores; vary block size and compare with naive IID intervals.

Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html

fields.topic_name: Information coefficient, calibration and stability by regime
fields.description:
Study guide: Compute rank information coefficient and probability calibration; break down scores by volatility regime, session and month.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html

fields.topic_name: Multiple-hypothesis testing and realistic effect sizes
fields.description:
Study guide: Demonstrate the winner's curse with many noisy signals; control for multiple comparisons and report material economic effects.

Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/tutorial/stats/hypothesis_tests.html

fields.topic_name: Test signal robustness across dates and instruments
fields.description:
Study guide: Re-evaluate a frozen signal on nonoverlapping days or instruments; report distribution of performance, not only overall average.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html

fields.topic_name: Compute uncertainty intervals and conduct ablation studies
fields.description:
Study guide: Add block-bootstrap confidence intervals around key metrics; perform feature ablations and write evidence for negative results.

Reference: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html

fields.topic_name: Forecast scores vs. trade decisions
fields.description:
Study guide: Separate probabilistic forecast, expected return, trading threshold and execution policy; test whether calibration is actionable.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html

fields.topic_name: Threshold selection and position sizing
fields.description:
Study guide: Choose trade threshold and capped position size using validation results; account for uncertainty, spread and forecast confidence.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html

fields.topic_name: Turnover, holding periods and risk constraints
fields.description:
Study guide: Measure turnover and time in market; implement holding limits, inventory bounds and drawdown triggers without future information.

Reference: https://www.quantstart.com/articles/Event-Driven-Backtesting-with-Python-Part-I/

fields.topic_name: Translate model forecasts into hypothetical long/short/flat signals
fields.description:
Study guide: Map model probabilities to long/short/flat decisions with a no-trade band; emit timestamped signals for a paper simulator.

Reference: https://www.quantstart.com/articles/Event-Driven-Backtesting-with-Python-Part-I/

fields.topic_name: Choose thresholds using training/validation data only
fields.description:
Study guide: Tune trade thresholds only on training/validation periods; freeze all parameters before a one-time final holdout evaluation.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html

fields.topic_name: Spread, fees, slippage, funding and adverse selection
fields.description:
Study guide: Model bid-ask crossing, commissions, tick sizes, funding when relevant, slippage and adverse selection; express PnL net of costs.

Reference: https://www.quantstart.com/articles/Event-Driven-Backtesting-with-Python-Part-I/

fields.topic_name: Latency, fills, queue position and market impact
fields.description:
Study guide: Distinguish quoted from executable fills; simulate latency and conservative queue assumptions; avoid filling at unseen future prices.

Reference: https://www.quantstart.com/articles/Event-Driven-Backtesting-with-Python-Part-I/

fields.topic_name: Sharpe, drawdown, turnover and capacity
fields.description:
Study guide: Calculate annualized Sharpe with correct sampling, max drawdown, turnover and capacity sensitivity; discuss unstable annualization.

Reference: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html

fields.topic_name: Develop a conservative event-driven simulator
fields.description:
Study guide: Build a timestamp-driven market-data/event/order/fill loop using public data and explicitly documented execution assumptions.

Reference: https://www.quantstart.com/articles/Event-Driven-Backtesting-with-Python-Part-I/

fields.topic_name: Report net results under pessimistic cost assumptions
fields.description:
Study guide: Sweep high fees, slippage and latency assumptions; tabulate net PnL, drawdown and break-even cost, including losing scenarios.

Reference: https://www.quantstart.com/articles/Event-Driven-Backtesting-with-Python-Part-I/

fields.name: LLMs and AI for quant research

fields.title: LLMs and AI for quant research
fields.deliverable: Small multimodal research experiment, or a documented failure analysis

fields.topic_name: Financial text embeddings and retrieval
fields.description:
Study guide: Learn embeddings and semantic retrieval; index public SEC filing passages and test query retrieval with source metadata.

Reference: https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/index

fields.topic_name: LLM evaluation, timestamps and point-in-time availability
fields.description:
Study guide: Define point-in-time availability using filing acceptance and publication timestamps; create an LLM evaluation set that checks citation correctness and hindsight leakage.

Reference: https://www.sec.gov/about/developer-resources

fields.topic_name: Combining text signals with numeric market features
fields.description:
Study guide: Join lagged text signals to numeric features using publication and market timestamps; evaluate incremental predictive value after transaction costs.

Reference: https://www.sec.gov/about/developer-resources

fields.topic_name: Prototype a public-news or filing-based signal experiment
fields.description:
Study guide: Retrieve public company filings and build a small labeled text-event dataset; record source URLs, release times and rate-limit compliance.

Reference: https://www.sec.gov/about/developer-resources

fields.topic_name: Test whether text features add incremental out-of-sample value
fields.description:
Study guide: Compare numeric-only and numeric-plus-text models on later unseen dates; include ablation and point-in-time audit.

Reference: https://huggingface.co/ProsusAI/finbert

fields.title: Publication and interview preparation
fields.deliverable: Portfolio, technical write-up and quant research interview narrative

fields.topic_name: Research reports and experiment reproducibility
fields.description:
Study guide: Write a research report with hypothesis, data provenance, validation, baselines, experiment log, results, uncertainty and limitations.

Reference: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~jrs/sins.html

fields.topic_name: Quant probability and statistics interview topics
fields.description:
Study guide: Practice probability, conditional expectation, confidence intervals, bias-variance, time series and mental estimation using quantitative examples.

Reference: https://www.statlearning.com/

fields.topic_name: Explaining model limitations and business relevance
fields.description:
Study guide: Explain why a signal may fail in production: regime shift, leakage, execution latency, adverse selection, crowding and data licensing.

Reference: https://www.quantstart.com/articles/Event-Driven-Backtesting-with-Python-Part-I/

fields.topic_name: Prepare polished GitHub repository and research report
fields.description:
Study guide: Publish sanitized code, environment lockfile, reproducible run commands, tables and model cards; exclude employer code or restricted market data.

Reference: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-readmes

fields.topic_name: Practice research defense and apply to suitable roles
fields.description:
Study guide: Prepare a 10-minute research defense: rationale, ablations, negative outcomes, execution assumptions and next experiments; rehearse critiques.

Reference: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~jrs/sins.html
